title: Complete Erdős Problem #1003: Consecutive Equal Totients (Work in Progress)

problemStatement.plain: Are there infinitely many solutions to φ(n) = φ(n+1), where φ is the Euler totient function? Erdős conjectured yes, and made the stronger claim that φ(n) = φ(n+1) = ... = φ(n+k) has infinitely many solutions for every k ≥ 1.
whyMatters: Euler's totient is central to number theory; equal consecutive values probe its fine multiplicative structure.
